active_paradigms.idea: Replace soft-extrema force descent with a direct antipodal line-packing SLSQP formulation
active_paradigms.description: The current program is a large batched continuation method: it starts mainly from seven antipodal directions, optimizes a soft minimum-minus-maximum log-distance objective, and sharpens the soft extrema through powers up to 1920. Its strength is broad deterministic basin coverage and stable scale/translation removal, which is why it nearly reaches the reference. Its limiting weakness is that the final objective remains a noisy subgradient approximation to a nonsmooth max/min problem, so it oscillates between changing active pairs rather than satisfying the active inequalities exactly. Exploit the apparent antipodal structure explicitly by optimizing seven unit vectors v_i and returning [v_1,...,v_7,-v_1,...,-v_7]. Introduce a scalar mu and call scipy.optimize.minimize once with method='SLSQP', objective mu, equality constraints ||v_i||^2=1, and inequalities mu-dot(v_i,v_j)>=0 and mu+dot(v_i,v_j)>=0 for every i<j. For an antipodal set the diameter is exactly 2 and the squared evaluator ratio is exactly (1-mu)/2, so this constrained problem directly optimizes the evaluator rather than a surrogate. Remove rotational null directions by fixing one direction to the z axis and one coordinate of a second direction, and use a fixed high-quality seven-line seed encoded in the program.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimize maximum absolute inner product mu; this maximizes the evaluator's squared ratio (1-mu)/2 for the antipodal construction and should remove the remaining roughly 0.1% soft-objective gap.
active_paradigms.cautions: Use analytic constraint Jacobians if possible and tight ftol/maxiter because the target improvement is very small. Verify all seven norms and all 21 absolute inner products after the call, then construct exact negatives so that dmax is reliably 2. A generic random initialization is unlikely to reach the correct contact graph; use one deterministic near-optimal seed, not repeated optimization calls.

active_paradigms.idea: Solve the active contact graph's KKT equations to obtain a high-precision stationary spherical code
active_paradigms.description: Treat the near-reference configuration as a seven-line packing problem rather than as 14 unconstrained particles. From a fixed close antipodal seed, determine offline which signed inner-product constraints attain the largest absolute value and hard-code that signed contact graph in the submitted program. Build a square KKT residual system containing unit-norm equations, equality equations s_ij dot(v_i,v_j)-mu=0 for the selected contacts, and tangential force-balance equations using one multiplier per contact. Call scipy.optimize.root once, preferably with method='lm' for an overdetermined residual formulation or method='hybr' after removing rotational gauge freedoms. The resulting root enforces equal active contacts and stationarity simultaneously, which is exactly what the current decaying soft-force iterations only approximate. Evaluate the actual maximum absolute dot product of the returned vectors, not merely the nominal mu, and return the corresponding seven vectors and their negatives.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical polishing of the active constraints and force balance, aiming to turn a nearly optimal soft-minimum solution into an accurately realized local optimum with a smaller true maximum coherence.
active_paradigms.cautions: This only works when the hard-coded contact graph and signs match the intended optimum; an incorrect graph may converge to a saddle or an infeasible code. Eliminate the three rotational degrees of freedom before making the system square, and reject roots with negative or implausibly large contact multipliers if the KKT convention requires nonnegative multipliers. The fixed approximate seed and graph should be obtained during development and embedded; do not run the current long continuation followed by root solving at evaluation time.

active_paradigms.idea: Use differential evolution on a compact seven-direction angular parameterization to test globally different line-packing basins
active_paradigms.description: The current population includes asymmetric 14-point starts, but its gradient flow is strongly attracted to the original antipodal/cubic-tetrahedral basin and may never discover a distinct contact graph. Parameterize seven unoriented unit directions by spherical angles, fixing the first direction and a rotational gauge so that only about eleven to fourteen bounded variables remain. Define the direct objective as max_{i<j}|dot(v_i,v_j)|; after optimization return the seven directions and their negatives. Invoke scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once with a fixed seed, a moderate population, deferred updating, workers=1 for reproducibility, and polish=False, so the single global call searches contact-graph topology rather than following the current soft-extrema trajectory. This objective is compact, bounded, and is exactly equivalent to the evaluator ratio within the antipodal family. Include a deterministic near-reference angular vector in the initial population if supported, while reserving the rest of that one population for broad exploration.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Global improvement of maximum coherence across qualitatively different seven-line contact graphs; it can either find a genuinely better code or establish a better seed for a later independently developed exact construction.
active_paradigms.cautions: Raw 42-coordinate differential evolution is prohibitively expensive and has redundant translation/scale/rotation modes; the reduced spherical-angle representation is essential. The max-absolute-dot objective is nonsmooth, so do not rely on the default local polishing stage. Bound runtime via maxiter and popsize, and always normalize reconstructed directions before returning them to avoid angular roundoff changing the diameter ratio.
